title: Your Share Trades Just Got Faster: Understanding the T+1 Settlement Cycle
description: When you buy or sell shares, the actual exchange of shares and money isn't instant; it happens later, in a process called settlement. India's stock market now.

faq.q: What is a "business day" in the context of T+1?
faq.a: A business day refers to a working day when the stock exchanges and banks are open. It excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays.

faq.q: Does T+1 apply to all types of investments in India?
faq.a: For equity shares traded on stock exchanges (like NSE and BSE), the T+1 settlement cycle is now standard. However, some other instruments like certain mutual funds or specific debt securities might have different settlement cycles, though many have also moved to T+1.

faq.q: What was the settlement cycle before T+1?
faq.a: Before T+1, India followed a T+2 settlement cycle, where trades were settled two business days after the transaction date.

faq.q: Is India planning to move to an even faster settlement cycle?
faq.a: Yes, SEBI is exploring the possibility of introducing a "T+0" (same-day) settlement cycle for a limited set of highly liquid stocks as a pilot project. This would mean trades settle on the very same day they are executed.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling shares within the same trading day, so the positions are squared off before market close. For such trades, the T+1 settlement cycle does not directly apply to the final delivery of shares or funds, as no net position remains at the end of the day for settlement. However, the overall market efficiency and liquidity improved by T+1 indirectly benefit all trading activities.
